findings.location: claude-workflow-plugin-lto2 (the correction recorded on the task) cross-checked against claude-workflow-plugin-8lc1
findings.evidence: GitHub Actions run 36232214628, headSha bff6cc4fc38ed35946a7d876de5a42337f126839, 2026-09-26, job 'L1 - bash unit tests'. One job's log carries all three of: (a) 'PASS: 1S.13.0d non-vacuity: en_US.UTF-8 is installed and really collates differently from C on this host'; (b) '=== approval-record-disclosure-claim.test.sh: 238 passed, 0 failed ==='; (c) 'SKIPPED: no locale installed on this host demonstrates the [a-v] collation exposure (tried en_US/en_GB/de_DE in both UTF-8 spellings)', emitted by runner-completeness.test.sh section 13w. The three L1 specs that actually failed in that run are design-artifact, design-conform and runner-completeness (gh run view 36232214628 --json jobs; --log | grep -E '^L1 .*--- .*: FAILED'). actions/runner-images Ubuntu2404-Readme.md lists the locales package 2.39-0ubuntu8.9 as installed in the IMAGE.
findings.description: The passage 'CI provisions NO locales (verified: no locale-gen, no locales package, no apt-get install anywhere in .github/workflows/test.yml), so those two WILL be red on CI. That is claude-workflow-plugin-8lc1' is wrong on all three clauses. (1) The runner IMAGE provisions locales, not the workflow; grepping test.yml is evidence about a FILE, not about a RUNTIME, which is the antipattern .claude/tests/README.md states as 'Do not count text to prove a claim about code'. (2) 1S.13.0d exists precisely to prove that host precondition and it PASSED on the real runner two days ago, along with 1S.13.1/.2/.3, with the whole spec green at 238/0. (3) 8lc1 is a different spec and a different exposure - its own title is 'runner-completeness skips the [a-v] collation section' - and its symptom appears in the SAME job alongside the passing 1S.13.0d, which is consistent rather than contradictory: en_US.UTF-8 can be installed and still not demonstrate a bracket-RANGE exposure. Nothing in the change set moves. What should move is the correction on lto2: on the available evidence 5384d49's 'last genuine L1 failure' line is not refuted by a locale gap, and nothing needs filing for 1S.13.0d/1S.13.1 because they are not red on CI.

findings.evidence: Driving the SHIPPED is_doc_only_path - extracted by the same three awk ranges .claude/scripts/tests/doc-only-classifier.test.sh uses (DOC-CONTENT-VETO, GOVERNING-ARTIFACT-VETO, the function itself), with _GOV_TOOL pointed at the real .claude/scripts/workflow-manifest.sh so the governing-artifact query is live - classifies docs/handover/v5.0.0-handover.md and docs/handover/v5.0.0-handover-addendum-2026-09-26.md DOC-ONLY, while docs/HOOKS.md (workflow), CLAUDE.md (runtime-contract), LESSONS.md (operator) and .claude/agents/qa.md (workflow) all return REVIEWABLE with the GOVERNING ARTIFACT diagnostic. workflow-manifest.sh declares no docs/handover row. Both handover files are clean under BANNED_CLAIM_PATTERN today (0 hits each), verified non-vacuously: the identical normalize-then-grep over a copy with a Tamper-Evident sentence appended returns 1.
findings.description: I agree with the decision (include, not exclude) over its alternative. The finding is that the change set records no residual for what the decision does not close. (a) A handover-only change set is doc-only, so it takes verify-before-stop.sh's F1 fast path and AUTO-APPROVES with no QA round while silently breaking the pin this decision just widened - which is exactly how d5be5a7 and 03bc940 landed. The discipline the decision relies on, one pin update in the same commit as each future handover, has no gate at the moment the handover commits; its only detector is a delayed red tier. (b) workflow-manifest.sh, the repo's own oracle for what the project declares as its own surface, has no docs/handover row, so the disclosure spec and the manifest now disagree about whether a handover is part of that surface - the disagreement class LESSONS.md already records against this file's own arc ('90 discovered against 138 declared'). (c) A future handover that needs to QUOTE the banned phrase in order to describe this work - the reason this spec file excludes ITSELF - would fire 1S.11, whose only remedy is rewriting a dated audit document, the 'own dishonesty' the file's own OUT-OF-SCOPE paragraph names for CHANGELOG entries. No change requested here, per the no-new-mechanisms constraint; this wants a follow-up task.

findings.evidence: The one sentence at :1311-1321 now reads '...+41(docs)+4(named root)+9(agents)+24(plugin-installed) = 102 raw, minus 10 overlaps ... = 92 (R6-F1: the previous formula here summed to 116 by duplicating a 24 term in place of one of the two 8s - the five categories actually sum to 100, not 116)'. Measured now by driving the extracted discover_* functions standalone against PROJECT_DIR: 8/8/8 script mirrors, 41 docs, 4 named root, 9 agents, 24 plugin-installed, union 92; 8+8+8+41+4+9+24 = 102.
findings.description: Leaving 100 is the RIGHT call on the number: 100 and 116 are a matched pair anchored at 39 docs (116-100 = 16 = 24-8, exactly the substitution the clause describes), so updating 100 alone would break the arithmetic relation the sentence exists to explain. The residual is the TENSE. Unlike the three other retained citations - :501 'MEASURED', :951 'QA demonstrated', :1490 'the 513j task record' - this clause is present-tense with no date anchor and sits three lines under a live '= 102 raw', so one sentence now states the raw sum as both 102 and 100. Minimal repair is one tense word: no number changes, no new mechanism. The commit message names the retained 116 but not the 100, and decisions[] does not mention it, so it reads as missed rather than decided.

findings.description: Not a defect - positive evidence for a filed one, recorded here because it closes a stated unknown rather than leaving it open. The implementer's context_coverage names 'whether the real GitHub Actions runner image has fr_FR.UTF-8' as its largest remaining unknown, and llm_observations says the gap 'plausibly reaches the real CI runner too but that was not verified either way'. It is verified now: fr_FR.UTF-8 is absent on the runner, so 1S.13.3 passes vacuously there for exactly the reason mnxp describes. This belongs on mnxp.
